solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rocket for American singer who loses a grand

indicators.note: something lost is taken away, so the letters of the phrase after it come out of the singer's full name

parts.note: Ariana Grande is a US pop singer
taken as written, the letters of these two words removed in order

explanation.surface: A US pop star seems to go down in the world, losing a thousand pounds and becoming a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes A, G, R, A, N, D out of ARIANA GRANDE in order, leaving the first five letters and the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: The European Space Agency's launch vehicles are named after this word, so it names a rocket.

clue.text: Scottish lawyer Five-O caught in a meeting

indicators.note: in means the numeral and letters go inside the meeting phrase

parts.note: a date is a meeting
V is the Roman numeral for five, followed by O
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Scottish lawyer is caught at a meeting with the Hawaii Five-O police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Five-O' recalls the TV police series, but it is V and O.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a barrister, a lawyer who pleads in the higher courts, has this title.

clue.text: Pinch 17 drivers, essentially, to get carrot

indicators.note: the essence of each word is its centre, so the middle letters of each are kept

parts.note: the number written out as a word

explanation.surface: A dare to steal seventeen drivers, with a carrot as reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the middle three letters of PINCH, SEVENTEEN and DRIVERS: INC, ENT, IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the carrot of carrot-and-stick is a reward that motivates.

clue.text: Lacking American good sense

parts.note: no, as in 'no money', means lacking
US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: A jibe that Americans have no common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is everyday British slang for practical common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym from Greek for mind, used in Britain for practical wit.

clue.text: Broccoli, possibly for the German copper coming back inside

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons

indicators.note: inside means the turned symbol goes within the German article

parts.note: der is the masculine form of 'the' in German

indicators.note: coming back means the symbol is read backwards

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A recipe-like line about broccoli and a German copper pan coming back into use.
explanation.walkthrough: Broccoli here is Albert 'Cubby' Broccoli, who made the James Bond films, not the vegetable; 'possibly' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubby Broccoli financed and made films, an example of a film-maker in the business sense.

clue.text: Very strict set-up or, occasionally, roguish

parts.note: a rig is a set-up or arrangement of equipment

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters are taken, every other one

explanation.surface: A very strict regime, or one that is now and then a bit roguish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes O, U, S, the second, fourth and sixth letters of 'roguish'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: exacting, stern and thorough.

clue.text: Pulling leg, which holds up paper?

parts.note: drawing a cart is pulling it
pin is slang for a leg

explanation.surface: Someone pulling another's leg, asking what holds up a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulling leg' looks like teasing, but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbtack, used to fix notices to a board, holds paper up.

clue.text: Squash resistance in such difficulties

indicators.note: in means the resistance letter is put among the jumbled ones
letters in difficulties are in disorder, so these are jumbled

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A squash player shows resistance in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such difficulties' makes CUSH; 'in' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to press hard or flatten something.

clue.text: Smelt bad and stretched again!

definitions.meaning: to eke is to stretch out, so ..., made to last a second time

explanation.surface: Something that stank once it was stretched a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as RE-EKED; the exclamation mark warns of the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is the past tense of stink; the second is a made-up word, eked again.

clue.text: Small vegetable is glossy

parts.note: S is the clothing size abbreviation for small
a leek is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A little vegetable with a shiny skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: smooth and shiny.

clue.text: Supply food cut up in small bottle

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the bottle

parts.note: a vial is a small glass bottle

indicators.note: something cut up is broken into pieces, so the letters of cut are jumbled

explanation.surface: Food rations chopped up and put in a little bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply food' is one verb phrase, the definition; 'up' is the anagram signal on 'cut', and 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to provide with provisions, an old word for feeding people.

clue.text: Tiny particle found in surgery on ear and lung

indicators.note: surgery cuts and rearranges, so the letters of the organs are reordered

explanation.surface: A speck discovered during an operation on someone's ear and lung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surgery on' rearranges EAR and LUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a small grain or speck of something.

clue.text: Preserves sacks

definitions.meaning: seals food in tins to keep it

explanation.surface: Jams and bags, or someone preserving and dismissing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are verbs: to tin food, and informally to fire someone from work.

clue.text: I'll soon explain strange white amber

indicators.note: strange means the letters of the two words are reordered into something odd

explanation.surface: Someone promises to explain an odd white form of amber.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first here though it reads like the speaker's promise, and the phrase means 'please be patient'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom asks a listener to wait patiently while the speaker gets to the point.

clue.text: Conduct group perjury session or stay in bed

definitions.meaning: read literally, have a session of falsehood, a lie, in company

explanation.surface: Two ways to spend a morning: run a group lying meeting, or sleep late.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: hold a 'lie-in' like a sit-in, where everyone lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sleeping late; the cryptic sense pictures a protest-style gathering for telling falsehoods.

clue.text: Ethnic group's test going around Belgium

indicators.note: going around means the test word encloses the country's letter

parts.note: a trial is a test
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: An ethnic group's examination is being taken around Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to a tribe, a people sharing ancestry and customs.

clue.text: Mushroom good in Bordeaux when filled with egg

indicators.note: filled with means the French word has the urging word put inside it

parts.note: bon is French for good, and Bordeaux is in France
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: A culinary note: a mushroom dish from Bordeaux, stuffed with egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushroom' and 'egg' are both verbs here, not foods.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs both mean to grow or spread fast, as mushrooms appear overnight.

clue.text: Delivery leaving on small sailing vessel

parts.note: to be off is to be leaving
a cutter is a small single-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A parcel being sent off on a little sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' is a cricket ball bowled, not a parcel; cricket is the British bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a ball that cuts in from the off side is a kind of bowled ball.

clue.text: Country left judgeable after odd losses

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: losing the odd letters means only the even-placed letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A country, left open to judgement after some strange losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after odd losses' keeps U, G, A, L from 'judgeable'.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Iberian nation west of Spain.

clue.text: Land workers have way up to vegetable hospital

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the street letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Farm labourers must take the road up to a vegetable hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' (a down clue read bottom to top) turns the street abbreviation round, and 'to' attaches it after the vegetable and hospital, though 'way' comes first in the clue; 'have' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rural labourers who work the land.

clue.text: Screen some episode reruns backwards

indicators.note: backwards means the hidden run of letters is read from right to left
some means only part of the words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: On screen, some episodes are rerun backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' finds SODERER in 'epiSODE RERuns'; 'backwards' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an ornamental screen or partition behind a church altar.

clue.text: Mix cards with extra-loud gun?

indicators.note: an extra letter is added inside the gun word

parts.note: a rifle is a gun
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: Shuffling a deck alongside a very noisy firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with extra' adds F (forte, loud in music) to RIFLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuffle a deck by flicking the corners of two halves so they interleave.

clue.text: Films usually use these timeless certificates

indicators.note: without time means the letter T, short for time, is removed

parts.note: films are usually made from written screenplays

explanation.surface: A note on what films use, and certificates that never date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' drops T from SCRIPTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrip is a certificate entitling the holder to shares or money.

clue.text: Poet seen in stake-out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A poet spotted during a police stakeout.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: John Keats, the English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Potatoes Dickens for one ate excessively

indicators.note: ate means the name takes the excessive abbreviation inside it, as food is taken in

parts.note: Charles Dickens, the novelist, is one example of a Charles
OTT, over the top, means excessively

explanation.surface: A novelist who gorged himself on potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is British shorthand for 'over the top'.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety of salad potato with this name is widely sold.

clue.text: Vote for one Republican per annum

parts.note: aye is a vote in favour
a means one

explanation.surface: Yearly voting for a single Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin per annum translates as each twelve months.

clue.text: People-carrier holds 500 sprouts

indicators.note: holds means the vehicle contains the numeral

parts.note: a bus carries people
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A people-carrier vehicle carrying 500 Brussels sprouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprouts' is a noun, the new shoots of a plant, not the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: young shoots or unopened flowers on a plant.

clue.text: Swedes and a bit of cabbage

indicators.note: a bit of means only part of the word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Swedes, the root vegetables, served with a bit of cabbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swedes' is the pop group's nationality, not the root vegetable (called rutabaga in North America).
explanation.definitionFit: The 1970s pop group came from Sweden, so its members are Swedes.

clue.text: Kill composer with lettuce

parts.note: to ice someone is slang for to kill them
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A murderer does away with a composer, using lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a crisp round variety of lettuce.

clue.text: Live in giant Dalai Lama?

indicators.note: in means the living word goes inside the giant

parts.note: a titan is a giant
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: The question whether the Dalai Lama lives inside a giant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the spiritual leader from Tibet, so an example of someone from there.

clue.text: Pepper season, when moose comes back for good

indicators.note: for means the turned animal replaces the letter for good

parts.note: spring is a season

indicators.note: comes back means the animal's name is read backwards

parts.note: the elk is the European name for the moose

explanation.surface: Seasoning with pepper, when the moose comes home for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pepper' and 'season' look like cooking terms; 'Pepper' is a verb meaning to scatter over. KLE, ELK turned by 'comes back', replaces G in SPRING.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper something is to scatter small drops or bits over it.

clue.text: Carpenter's mate was holding hands for all to see

indicators.note: holding means the word was encloses the other letters

parts.note: left and right hands, L and R
U is the British film certificate for a universal audience, so suitable for all

explanation.surface: A carpenter's workmate was openly holding hands.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's poem 'The Walrus and the Carpenter' the two walk together; U is the British film rating meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: In Carroll's poem, the tusked sea mammal is the companion of the Carpenter.
